text:
Situation: Spironolactone supply is constrained across Corvale sites. Corvale East has 8.5 days of 100 mg tablets and 17.9 days of 25 mg tablets. Corvale General holds 27.1 and 22.1 days across two listings. Corvale Lakeside has 10 days of 25 mg tablets. Pfizer Inc. spironolactone tablets are posted on FDA's shortage list as To Be Discontinued effective 2025-12-10.

Why (FDA record): Our supply includes product labeled by Bryant Ranch Prepack from plant FEI 1000519407. FDA inspected that plant on 2009-06-11 and classified it OAI, with classification known 2009-09-09. FDA issued a Warning Letter to the plant on 2010-04-08. Subsequent inspections in 2010, 2011, 2013, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2024, and 2026 were all classified VAI. The most recent inspection ended 2026-07-16 and was classified VAI, with classification known 2026-10-14.

Our position: Current inventory will not sustain all sites beyond three weeks. Pfizer's discontinuation removes a major national source. Alternative manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list today, but their labels do not identify plants we can verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place immediate orders with A-S Medication Solutions, Accord Healthcare Inc., Advagen Pharma Ltd., American Health Packaging, and Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC for both strengths; buyer approves purchase orders.
2. Buyer to request plant FEI numbers and current inspection classifications from each supplier; buyer and quality assurance manager approve vendor qualification.
3. Inventory manager to allocate incoming stock first to Corvale Lakeside and Corvale East 100 mg; inventory manager approves distribution plan.
4. Pharmacy director to report weekly days-on-hand by site and strength to P&T committee; pharmacy director approves reporting cadence.

Not recommended: Initiate therapeutic substitutions or protocol changes; those are clinical decisions for the treating clinicians and the committee.
